newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends down on crop condition, fund sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends down on crop condition, fund sales.

text.p: Signs of improvement in the condition of the U.S. wheat crop and heavy commodity fund sales caused CBOT wheat futures to end with moderate losses Tuesday, floor traders said.

On Monday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture showed the condition of the hard red winter wheat crop--damaged by freezing spring temperatures--improving slightly. USDA showed modest improvement in the Kansas, Texas and Oklahoma crops.
However, some market observers cautioned that it is too early to fully determine the impact that an unseasonable spring freeze had on the wheat.

"I think...you have to remember that these ratings represent a judgment of what the plant looks like that week, not how much it will yield," said Doug Hjort, president of Hjort and Associates in Adel, Iowa.
Hjort, a former Montana wheat farmer, said that he had seen crops hit by freezing temperatures develop nicely through the growing season only to produce no grain at harvest.
Liquidation in May and heavy fund selling pressed on nearbys. Funds sold up to 30 million bushels, traders said.
Wheat futures ended down 11-1/4 to two cents per bushel, with July down 8-3/4 at $4.02-1/2.
Reports from tour participants on a wheat crop tour moving through northern and central Kansas supported the USDA data.
Most crop scouts on the Wheat Quality Council's hard red wheat tour were forecasting yields equal to or above those of last year in those areas and incidence of disease was generally low.
The tour has yet to go through southwest Kansas where the unusual April freeze was said to hit wheat the hardest.
Forecasts for drought-relieving rains throughout Europe also contributed to the wheat market's weakness, traders said.
Support in wheat stemmed from commercial buying throughout the session, floor sources said.
Cargill, Inc bought eight million bushels and Continental Grain bought one million July, traders said.
"These (wheat) prices are going to look pretty good to a flour mill that had to pay $7.00 (per bushel) last year," said a CBOT wheat trader.

On the day, funds sold an estimated 15 million bushels of wheat, traders said. Prudential Securities sold 2.5 million July, LIT sold three million July and Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold three million July, sources said.
In options trade, Spike Trading bought 400 July $3.60 puts and sold 400 July $3.70 puts, floor sources said.
Volume was estimated at 22,000 contracts. That figure was slightly higher than Monday's final volume of 21,939 contracts, according to CBOT data.
